sources.name: Barrett Technology, LLC — current WAM configuration table
Barrett Technology, LLC — linked WAM family datasheet; contradictory date labels
Barrett Technology, LLC — system-components matrix, updated 17 January 2019

highlights: The current WAM table explicitly gives WAM 4-DOF Standard: 4 kg payload, 3 m/s peak endtip velocity and 1 mm repeatability. These are separate ratings, not a tested simultaneous full-load operating point or absolute positioning accuracy.
The 4-DOF arm is listed at 25 kg. The shared 1 m reach and reported 3.5 cubic-metre workspace do not give a complete body envelope, while 50 W active power does not establish battery endurance.

Gearless cable drives support backdrivability, force control and direct-teach/trajectory playback. Hand, force/torque sensors, gimbals and Puck controllers retain component roles; extra finger axes or gripper capacity do not increase the base arm payload. Performance upgrades are kept in their own named configurations.

highlights: Supports the patient's arm weight during interactive upper-limb activities
Haptic forces can assist or resist movement, with backdrivability in three planes
Therapist-selected activities and built-in strength assessments provide session scoring

The manufacturer advertises about 60 seconds for base setup and left/right exchange, while optional BurtWrist has its own under-90-second setup claim. These are setup claims, not battery runtime or charging time; three backdrivability planes are not a measured joint count.

The same page lists eighteen activities in one section and twenty in another. The library count remains unresolved rather than chosen as a single current total; named games are software activities, not robot models.

Optional BurtWrist adds motorized pronation/supination, graded grip sensing and passive, active, assisted or resisted modes. It is an addition to Burt, not independently identified as another complete base robot.

Therapists select activity and difficulty, with session scoring and strength-assessment tools. BurtCare covers software/assessment updates, service and subscription support; testimonials and manufacturer regulatory/safety language are not independent clinical efficacy, approval or absolute-safety verification.

highlights: Barrett distinguishes its medical and drive-systems activities. Burt is a therapist-controlled rehabilitation platform; WAM is a force-controllable robotic-arm family with four- and seven-axis configurations and a separate historical gimbals/master package.

Current WAM table options distinguish Standard, High Speed/Ultra High Speed, High Payload and High Precision. Their ratings are not combined into unsupported hybrid configurations or independently verified comparative superiority.

portfolioDecisions.gimbalsOwnership: Third configuration explicitly named in linked WAM PDF and 2019 system-components matrix; distinct from 7-DOF wrist configuration. Do not inherit masses, payload, speed or exact end reach of ordinary WAM configurations.
